label: super-kapitsa
display: Kapitsa (LiLiCorr drafter, GPU + Neural Engine prefill)
note: Kapitsa's default settings on NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint read as stored (NVFP4 routed and shared experts, FP8 Mamba projections / attention / LM head, BF16 latent projections quantized to Q8_0 at load, BF16 router and embedding), with NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter named explicitly (--dflash <folder>/dflash, the folder --dflash auto finds; a missing drafter fails the run instead of decoding plain). Prefill splits the FP8 Mamba projections and the NVFP4 shared expert between the GPU and the Neural Engine (compiled in the background after start; the warm-up and decode phases come first). --slots 1 for parity with the others' single sequence. The folder is Kapitsa's store copy of nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 @ 59b87216 with nvidia/...-NVFP4-LiLiCorr @ 292bf1ef in dflash/ (kapitsa pull super-vl). Reference prompt lengths 4183 / 16513: the corpus prompts through this model's tokenizer and chat template (transformers apply_chat_template, enable_thinking false, 8 nonces each: 4180-4184 / 16512-16516).

label: super-kapitsa-plain
note: The same server with --dflash none: plain one-token decoding (Kapitsa does not run Super-VL's MTP head yet), for comparison with the other engines' plain configurations. Everything else as super-kapitsa.

label: super-mlxvlm
version: mlx-vlm git main 73d366e (unreleased; its metadata says 0.7.8), mlx 0.32.4
version_cmd: import importlib.metadata as m, json; d = m.distribution('mlx-vlm'); print('mlx-vlm', d.version, d.read_text('direct_url.json'), 'mlx', m.version('mlx'))
note: mlx-vlm on the same NVIDIA NVFP4 folder Kapitsa reads (NVFP4 experts kept as MLX nvfp4 with their global scales, FP8 layers converted to BF16 at load). Unreleased build: mlx-vlm git main @ 73d366e (2026-10-17), because Super-VL support (model type nemotron_h_omni and its native MTP drafter, PR #2528, merged 2026-10-16) came after the latest release, 0.7.8, which refuses the model ('Model type nemotron_h_omni not supported'). MLX_VLM_MAIN_PYTHON = a venv with that commit (mlx 0.32.4). Automatic prefix caching on (APC_ENABLED=1, in memory only), mlx-vlm's own switch for reusing a conversation's prefix in follow-up turns (off by default); 2048-token prefill steps (its default, stated); one sequence at a time. The request's model id is the path the server was started with.

label: super-mlxvlm-mtp
display: mlx-vlm server (git main, native MTP, block 4)
note: As super-mlxvlm, with the checkpoint's own MTP head as the drafter (--draft-model = the same folder, --draft-kind mtp), the path PR #2528 added and benchmarked. Block size 4: the fastest of 2-6 in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s: block 2 39.5 / 41.9, 3 44.1 / 47.2 (PR #2528's setting), 4 47.4 / 50.4, 5 45.6 / 50.8, 6 39.6 / 42.7; the drafter's own default is 2).

label: super-omlx
display: oMLX (community MLX 4-bit, text only, no speculation)
note: oMLX 0.7.1rc1 cannot read NVIDIA's checkpoint: it is model type nemotron_h_omni, which oMLX routes to its bundled mlx-vlm 0.7.8, and that release has no Super-VL. Its supported path is a text-only MLX conversion through its bundled mlx-lm (nemotron_h with LatentMoE): rapid-mlx/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-MLX-4bit @ 01678903 (MLX affine 4-bit g64 from NVIDIA's BF16 weights, embedding 8-bit, LM head / router / latent projections BF16; 69.5 GB), the only text-only MLX 4-bit conversion of the model. That repo omits the MTP head and oMLX's DFlash path covers no Nemotron-H model, so oMLX runs it without speculation. Its README says Rapid-MLX applies a 'precision adapter' that stock loaders do not; mlx-lm's loader reads the files as they are. Cache flags as in omlx.json.

label: super-mlxlm
note: mlx-lm 0.32.2 refuses NVIDIA's checkpoint ('Model type nemotron_h_omni not supported'), and its nemotron_h model would not read the ModelOpt NVFP4 / per-tensor FP8 tensors of the language model either (its sanitize only stacks the experts' weights). It runs the same text-only MLX 4-bit folder as super-omlx (rapid-mlx @ 01678903), with the mlx-lm.json settings: prompt cache 4 sequences / 8 GB, 2048-token prefill steps. No MTP or drafter path in mlx-lm.

label: super-llamacpp
note: llama.cpp v0.7.0 (build b11669, the latest release; Super-VL / Nemotron omni support, PR #30520, is in it) on ggml-org's official GGUF of the model: ggml-org/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-GGUF @ 3c91ad1b, Q4_0 (71.8 GB; converted from NVIDIA's BF16 weights). That repo's other quantizations are NVFP4 (76.9 GB), which llama.cpp's Metal backend has no kernels for (matmuls would fall back to the CPU), Q8_0 (128.5 GB) and BF16, so Q4_0 is its 4-bit choice on a Mac. Settings as llama.cpp.json: one 32K slot, all layers on the GPU, flash attention, 2048-token batches, -lm none so the weights count in the footprint, the chat template inside the GGUF with --jinja, --min-p 0, prompt cache and 32 context checkpoints (the Mamba layers' state for prefix reuse).

label: super-llamacpp-mtp1
note: MTP speculative decoding with the model's MTP head, which ggml-org ships as a separate GGUF next to the trunk (mtp-...-Q4_0.gguf, 2.27 GB: the file llama.cpp's own -hf ...:Q4_0 download pairs with the Q4_0 trunk). Each extra verified row of this top-22-of-512 MoE reads up to 22 more experts, so n-max 1, 2 and 3 are all measured.

label: super-llamacpp-mtp3
note: As super-llamacpp-mtp1 with n-max 3, llama-server's default depth.

label: super-llamacpp-lilicorr
note: NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter as ggml-org converted it (lilicorr-...-NVFP4.gguf, 1.35 GB, from nvidia/...-NVFP4-LiLiCorr), run by llama.cpp's DFlash path (PR #30506: --spec-type draft-dflash; the GGUF's lilicorr.* keys select LiLiCorr's head). The only GGUF of the drafter is NVFP4, which the Metal backend has no kernels for. n-max 7 = the drafter's full block (block_size 8); llama-server's default n-max 3 caps it at 3 drafts. Smoke tests (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s): n-max 3 25.2 / 23.5, n-max 7 30.0 / 29.4, against 36.9 / 35.8 without a drafter, with about 4.7 tokens accepted per cycle.

label: super-ollama-mlx
display: Ollama MLX runner (NVIDIA NVFP4 tag + MTP head, adaptive depth)
log_grep: starting runner|ollama runner|mlx runner is ready
note: Ollama 0.40.6's official tag for Super on Apple silicon: NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint with its MTP head (text only), served by Ollama's MLX runner with its built-in adaptive MTP (no knobs). Dedicated server with 32K context, one slot.

label: super-lmstudio
note: LM Studio's staff pick for Super-VL is GGUF only (lmstudio-community Q4_K_M), so it runs on LM Studio's llama.cpp engine at its defaults; its MLX engine cannot load NVIDIA's checkpoint (nemotron_h_omni).

label: super-mlxserve
note: mlx-serve 26.10.2 cannot read NVIDIA's checkpoint (nemotron_h_omni); it runs the text-only MLX 4-bit conversion oMLX and mlx-lm read (rapid-mlx/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-MLX-4bit @ 01678903, model type nemotron_h), which has no MTP head, so without speculation.

label: super-mtplx
note: MTPLX 2.12.2 cannot read NVIDIA's checkpoint (nemotron_h_omni); it runs the text-only MLX 4-bit conversion oMLX and mlx-lm read (rapid-mlx/...-MLX-4bit @ 01678903), which has no MTP head, so without MTP (--no-mtp).
